data.why: the repo ships no example gaze/pupil CSVs (only CLI synthetic generators and fixtures for unrelated calibration/validation JSON checks), so demo_gaze.csv/demo_pupil.csv were hand-written in the t,x,y / t,size,unit schema itrace.io expects, with a fixation-saccade-fixation gaze trace (two saccades of different amplitude/direction, a short NaN gaze dropout, and small fixational jitter) and a matching pupil trace (a blink NaN gap and a saccade-locked dilation/decay bump), since the repo's real Streamlit entry point (src/itrace/dashboard.py:run_app) is only a title-and-one-line stub with no uploader or plots.

goals: Load a recorded or synthetic gaze CSV and inspect the x/y trajectory and velocity trace
Detect fixations and saccades with I-VT and review amplitude, direction, duration and peak velocity per saccade
Detect microsaccades (Engbert & Kliegl) and inspect the scanpath encoding
Fit and inspect the main sequence (amplitude vs. peak velocity power law)
Preprocess and inspect pupil traces (blink interpolation, dilation response, summary statistics)

Check detector recovery against synthetic ground truth across stress domains (clean desktop, webcam jitter, head-pose drift, low-light dropout) and review recording-quality diagnostics (dropout fraction, sampling-interval jitter)

review.summary: The tree captures what the analysis interface is for: get a session in, tune and review event detection against truth, read the main sequence, pupil and quality summaries, and validate the detector across synthetic stress domains. Most cited screens match. It needs fixes before filing: t8 makes a misleading scanpath claim, two branch types are wrong, a crash is filed as a workflow step, f2 and f6 have wording slips, f4 and f6 are generic widgets rather than real features, and it doesn't say that this page was written by the run rather than shipped by the repo.
